{"query": "What are the dominant narratives about immigration in the corpus?"}

answer.answer:
The corpus clusters around a legality frame: several posts insist on a sharp distinction between "legal" and "illegal" immigration and that illegal entry is never justified [T4-006133](#T4-006133) [T4-005475](#T4-005475) [T4-006969](#T4-006969), with one framing illegal immigration as a public-safety issue and mocking liberals [T4-005893](#T4-005893), and another linking it to crime via a mother blaming sanctuary cities for her son's killing [T4-000416](#T4-000416).

A second narrative is enforcement and restriction: calls for a "deportation force" [T4-006695](#T4-006695), mockery of Obama-era DHS border rhetoric [T4-004871](#T4-004871), a story of an undocumented immigrant surprised by deportation after an ICE check-in [T4-007235](#T4-007235), a report that the Trump administration considered using the National Guard for immigration roundups [T4-006611](#T4-006611), and ridicule of attempts to enter via Canada because of its immigration policy [T4-005928](#T4-005928). Trump-era policy is contested from both sides, criticized as "crackpot" [T4-000729](#T4-000729) and compared with Clinton's position in debate coverage [T4-004357](#T4-004357).

A third narrative is data/news coverage: profiles of US residents without legal status [T4-007836](#T4-007836), state-by-state immigration growth [T4-004321](#T4-004321), US–Mexico diplomatic friction over immigration [T4-006718](#T4-006718), and a 2014 report that the US lifted a ban on immigrants with terrorism links, one post adding "IT'S NOT ABOUT ISLAM" [T4-003938](#T4-003938) [T4-003608](#T4-003608). A few posts are too fragmentary to classify [T4-003955](#T4-003955) [T4-005190](#T4-005190) [T4-000980](#T4-000980).
